eyebrow-microblading.summary: Semi-permanent hair-like pigment strokes tattooed into the brows for fuller, darker, more defined brows that last up to about two years.

quick.overview:
Microblading fills thin, sparse or uneven brows with fine hair-like strokes of pigment, giving thicker, darker, more defined brows that are visible as soon as the session is done. Men who want stronger brows discuss it for that reason.

A technician draws the strokes with a handheld tool into the upper layer of the dermis, where the pigment stays visible until it fades. Published literature is mostly reviews and case reports of complications, and forum opinions vary on how natural the result looks.
quick.how: It is done as a salon or clinic session, with the technician choosing a pigment shade and brow shape to match your face. Results last up to about two years, with a touch-up usually suggested around six weeks later and then every 12 to 18 months. People often keep brows trimmed and groomed around the new shape.
quick.risks: Case reports describe granulomatous reactions, sarcoidosis, allergic contact dermatitis, cellulitis and a reported mpox transmission. As with any tattoo, unclean equipment is the main route to infection. Regulation varies by region, and people with pigment allergies or skin conditions around the brows may want to avoid it.

angle.text: Microblading tattoos hair-like pigment strokes into thin or uneven brows, so fuller, darker, more defined brows are visible straight away and last up to about two years. Men weigh how natural the strokes look against the gain in density. Published literature is mostly case reports of side effects.

powder-ombre-nano-brows.summary: Machine-applied semi-permanent brow tattoo that gives a soft, shaded, make-up-like fill for fuller, defined brows that fade over months to a couple of years.

quick.overview:
Powder, ombre and nano brows are salon names for semi-permanent brow tattoos that fill sparse or uneven brows with a soft, shaded finish that looks like brow makeup. The result is visible right after the session.

A machine places pigment, commonly iron-oxide based, into the upper skin layers with fine needles, rather than drawing single hair strokes by hand as in microblading. Powder and ombre styles are usually lighter at the front and darker toward the tail, and nano uses very fine needles for a subtler result. No studies specific to these styles were found, so what is known comes from general information on cosmetic tattooing.
quick.how: People book a salon session, pick a shade and shape, and return for touch-ups. Because the pigment sits shallow it fades over months to a couple of years. It suits people who like a defined, filled-in brow look without drawing it on each day.
quick.risks: Reported risks of cosmetic tattooing include infection, reactions to pigment, granulomas, pigment migration and colour change. In the US there is no federal regulation or standard for testing the ink, and rules vary elsewhere.

angle.text: These semi-permanent brow tattoos give a soft, shaded fill that looks like brow makeup, so brows look fuller and more defined from the moment the session ends. They are popular salon services and fade over months to a couple of years. No dedicated studies exist for these styles.

henna-brows.summary: A plant-dye stain on brow hair and skin that darkens and fills in brows for days to weeks, without a tattoo.

quick.overview:
Henna brows use a plant-based paste to stain the brow hairs and the skin underneath, giving darker, more filled-in, defined brows with no tattoo involved. The stain is visible immediately.

Lawsone, the dye in henna, binds to keratin in hair and skin once the dried leaves are powdered and made into a paste. Skin stains typically fade by exfoliation within one to three weeks, and no clinical studies of the brow treatment were found.
quick.how: It is a short salon service where the paste is applied to the brows and left on before being removed. Results are temporary, so people repeat it every few weeks, often alongside regular brow trimming and shaping.
quick.risks: Pure henna rarely causes reactions, but additives in commercial pastes have been linked to them. Products sold as 'black henna' may contain PPD, which can cause severe allergic reactions and scarring. G6PD deficiency is a noted danger, and the FDA has not approved henna for direct skin use.

angle.text: Henna stains the brow hairs and the skin beneath them, so brows look darker, fuller and more defined straight away. The stain lasts days to weeks and is a surface effect you can see directly.

brow-shaving-brow-reshaping-for-tilt.summary: Trimming, shaving or reshaping the brows to change the angle of the eye area, aiming for a more tilted, 'hunter eyes' look; cheap and reversible.

quick.overview:
Looksmaxxers reshape or trim their brows to make the eye area look more upward-angled, aiming for a positive tilt and a 'hunter eyes' look. The change is visible as soon as the hair is cut, and it costs almost nothing.

Changing the brow's outline changes the line the eye reads against, which proponents say alters the apparent angle of the eye. No studies were found testing whether trimming changes perceived tilt; the published research is on surgical brow shaping and lifting.
quick.how: People remove or trim hair with tweezers, wax, thread, scissors or a razor, and some redraw the shape with brow makeup. Because hair regrows, the shape is maintained with regular grooming, and many try small changes first.
quick.risks: Hair generally regrows, so changes are temporary, though over-trimming or over-plucking can leave gaps that take time to fill back in. Surgical brow shaping carries standard operative risks and is a separate matter from grooming.

angle.text: Trimming or reshaping the brows changes the line above the eye, which looksmaxxers use to make the eye area look more upward-tilted and 'hunter'-like. The change is cheap, reversible and visible right away. Its effect on perceived tilt has not been studied.

brow-thread-lift.summary: Threads placed under the skin to raise the brow tail without surgery, giving a lifted, more open eye area.

quick.overview:
A brow thread lift raises the outer part of the eyebrow using threads placed under the skin, giving a lifted brow and a more open-looking eye area without a surgical brow lift. The lift is visible after the procedure.

The threads are anchored in the brow and forehead tissue to hold the brow tail higher. Surgical lifts reposition tissue through incisions, and botulinum toxin raises the brow by relaxing opposing muscles. No completed trials were found; a registered study plans to examine how long thread-assisted brow suspension lasts.
quick.how: It is done in a clinic as a minimally invasive procedure and is offered as a middle option between toxin and surgery. How long the lift holds is the open question for people considering it.
quick.risks: Specific complication rates for brow threads were not found. Brow lifts in general carry risks such as infection, bleeding and numbness.

angle.text: Threads are placed to suspend and raise the tail of the brow without surgery, so the brow sits higher and the eye area looks more open once the procedure is done. It is offered as an alternative to surgical brow lifts. Evidence on how long it lasts is thin.

orbital-rim-implants.summary: Silicone or porous implants set along the lower orbital rim to add bony support under the eye and smooth hollows, discussed as a longer-lasting option than filler.

quick.overview:
Orbital rim implants are synthetic implants placed on the bony rim under the eye to reduce hollowing and support the lower lid, giving a smoother, more supported under-eye. They are sometimes combined with cheek (malar) implants. Hardmaxxing forums discuss them as a durable alternative to filler.

A silicone, porous polyethylene or similar implant, standard or custom-made from CT scans, is placed under the periosteum of the rim and secured, adding projection to the bony support. Published data on cosmetic use are limited, and much of the satisfaction data comes from malar implants.
quick.how: It is a surgical procedure done under anaesthesia by a facial surgeon, with recovery of several weeks. Forum discussion centres on standard versus custom designs and on pairing with cheek implants.
quick.risks: Reported complications include lower eyelid malposition, infection, contour irregularities and implant extrusion, and rarely nerve injury or sinus fistula. It is major facial surgery, so people with active infection or unrealistic expectations are typically advised against it.

angle.text: Implants along the lower orbital rim build bony support under the eye and smooth hollows and tear troughs, a change you can see once healed. It is promoted as more durable than fillers. Published data on cosmetic use is thin.

infraorbital-rim-zygomatic-filler.summary: Hyaluronic acid filler placed around the under-eye rim and cheekbone to add support and a more structured mid-face; temporary and technically delicate.

quick.overview:
Infraorbital rim and zygomatic filler adds volume under the eye and over the cheekbone for a deeper-set, more supported eye area and a more structured mid-face. The change is visible after treatment.

Gel, usually hyaluronic acid, is injected into the tissue around the lower orbital rim and cheek to add volume and projection. Evidence consists of small pilot studies, anatomical studies and complication reviews, and researchers are studying depth, vessel locations and fat patterns to refine placement.
quick.how: It is done in a clinic as a non-surgical injection treatment, and results are temporary, so people repeat it over time. It is often discussed as a lower-commitment step before implants.
quick.risks: Common effects are bruising, swelling, a blue-grey tint and contour irregularities. Rarely, filler entering an artery can cause tissue death or permanent vision loss. Fillers are regulated as medical devices in the US, and the under-eye area is anatomically delicate.

angle.text: Hyaluronic acid filler around the lower orbital rim and cheekbone fills hollows and adds support under the eyes, giving a more structured mid-face that is visible after treatment. The result is temporary.

fat-grafting-lower-eyelid-tear-trough.summary: Your own fat moved into the under-eye hollow to soften the tear trough and smooth the lid-to-cheek transition.

quick.overview:
Fat grafting takes a small amount of your own fat from another body area and places it in the hollow between the lower lid and cheek, softening the tear trough and giving a smoother transition. Forum users discuss it as a longer-lasting alternative to hyaluronic acid filler.

The harvested fat is processed and injected as volume under the thin eyelid skin, filling the depression. Proponents also say the transferred tissue may improve skin quality, which researchers are still studying. A systematic review found the literature was mostly case reports and retrospective case series.
quick.how: It is a surgical procedure done by a surgeon, sometimes combined with lower blepharoplasty. Fat is collected, prepared and placed in the eye area, with results settling as swelling goes down.
quick.risks: Reported problems with fat grafting include swelling, bruising, infection, lumpy or uneven contours, partial reabsorption of the fat and fat necrosis. The thin eyelid skin makes irregularities more visible, and results can shift with major weight change.

angle.text: Fat from elsewhere on your body is placed in the under-eye hollow, so the tear trough softens and the lid-to-cheek transition looks smoother. Evidence comes mostly from case series.

transconjunctival-lower-blepharoplasty.summary: Lower-eyelid surgery through an incision inside the lid, with no outer scar, to remove or reposition under-eye fat bags for a smoother, less puffy look.

quick.overview:
In transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty the surgeon works through a cut on the inner surface of the lower eyelid, so there is no visible external scar. It removes or moves the fat that bulges as under-eye bags and smooths the lid-cheek transition, giving a flatter, less puffy under-eye once swelling settles.

Orbital fat is either removed or repositioned along the infraorbital rim to fill the tear trough hollow. It is an established technique in the plastic-surgery literature, including combinations with fat grafting; published support comes largely from surgeon case series.
quick.how: It is done under anaesthesia by a surgeon and suits people with fat bags and little or no excess skin. Where skin laxity is present, an additional procedure may be needed, and some surgeons add a canthopexy or canthoplasty.
quick.risks: Swelling and bruising are common and usually settle over several weeks. Eyelid malposition is a recognised complication of lower blepharoplasty in general. It is a surgical procedure that should be done by a qualified surgeon.

angle.text: Surgery through the inside of the lower lid removes or repositions under-eye fat for a flatter, less puffy lower lid, with no external scar. The visible change is the result itself once swelling settles.

plasma-pen-blepharoplasty.summary: A handheld plasma device used on eyelid skin to tighten it without cutting; popular in DIY and salon circles, with almost no published clinical research.

quick.overview:
Plasma pen blepharoplasty uses a handheld plasma device to tighten loose or wrinkled eyelid skin without surgery, aiming for tighter, more lifted-looking eyelids. It is marketed as a non-surgical alternative to eyelid surgery.

The pen creates tiny points of controlled skin injury, and proponents say the skin then contracts and rebuilds collagen. On looksmax.org one poster lists the eyelids, nasal folds, forehead and neck as target areas. No clinical studies of the technique on eyelids were found.
quick.how: People either book clinic treatments or buy inexpensive devices; one forum poster describes devices at roughly 40 to 60 dollars and clinic sessions at 400 to 1,900 dollars.
quick.risks: Eyelid skin is very thin and close to the eye, and scarring is a concern commonly raised about plasma treatments in this area. No safety data for eyelid use were found. Home use of devices on this area is the riskiest route.

angle.text: A plasma pen is promoted in DIY and salon circles as a way to tighten loose eyelid skin for a tighter, better eye area without surgery, and cheap home devices are discussed. Almost no published clinical research covers its use on eyelids.

polynucleotide-eye-filler.summary: Polynucleotide injections into the thin skin around the eyes aimed at fresher, smoother, less crepey lower-lid skin.

quick.overview:
Polynucleotide eye filler is an injection of polynucleotide-based product into the thin skin around the eyes, aimed at better-quality, smoother, less crepey skin rather than adding large volume.

Proponents describe polynucleotides as stimulating skin repair and hydration. Very little documentation exists for the periorbital use; a registered observational study of a periorbital rejuvenation procedure (n=29) does not name the product.
quick.how: It is done as a clinic injection treatment, and the aim is gradual skin improvement rather than an immediate contour change.
quick.risks: Injections near the eye carry the general risks of periorbital injectables, including bruising, swelling and lumpiness, and the thin skin shows irregularities. No specific safety data for this use were found.

angle.text: Polynucleotide injections around the eyes aim to improve skin quality, so thin, crepey lower-lid skin looks smoother and fresher over time. Very little published research covers this eye-area use.

eyelid-rf-laser-tightening.summary: Fractional lasers and radiofrequency devices that use heat to firm loose eyelid skin and soften fine lines without surgery; small studies show modest improvement.

quick.overview:
Eyelid laser or radiofrequency tightening uses controlled heat to make loose or crepey eyelid skin firmer and smoother, as a non-surgical alternative to blepharoplasty. Fractional lasers are the best documented.

Fractional lasers create microscopic zones of thermal injury, and the tightening is attributed to the healing and remodelling that follows. Published work includes a prospective single-blinded study of ablative fractional CO2 laser on lower-eyelid laxity in 25 subjects, reports of non-ablative resurfacing improving tightening and eyelid aperture, and a registered trial comparing fractional laser and ultrasound. Radiofrequency-specific studies were not found.
quick.how: Treatment is typically a short series of sessions in a clinic, with downtime that depends on how aggressive the laser is. Marked laxity is usually managed surgically instead.
quick.risks: Treating skin this close to the eye requires eye protection and expertise. Laser resurfacing carries general risks such as redness, swelling and pigment change. Marked laxity from tendon looseness is treated surgically, for example with a tarsal strip procedure.

angle.text: Fractional laser or radiofrequency heat triggers skin remodelling that firms lax eyelid skin and softens fine lines without surgery. Small studies show modest improvement; heavy laxity is usually treated surgically.

vitamin-k-eye-cream.summary: Topical vitamin K marketed for under-eye dark circles with a blood-vessel component, to lighten the bluish look.

quick.overview:
Vitamin K eye cream is applied under the eyes and marketed for dark circles with a vascular or bruise-like look, with the aim of a lighter, brighter under-eye. Vitamin K is a fat-soluble vitamin known for its role in blood clotting.

Proponents link that clotting role to reducing blood pooling beneath thin skin. No clinical studies of topical vitamin K for dark circles were found. Dark circles have many causes, including anatomy, pigmentation, allergies, eye rubbing, medications and thin skin.
quick.how: It is used as an ordinary cosmetic cream, applied under the eyes as part of a skincare routine, often alongside sunscreen and other eye-area products.
quick.risks: Reference material notes no known toxicity from high oral intakes of K1 or K2, while intravenous injection can cause severe reactions; those findings concern oral and injected forms, not creams. As with any product near the eyes, irritation is possible.

angle.text: Vitamin K eye cream is marketed to fade the bluish look of under-eye circles that have a visible-vessel component, for a brighter under-eye. The sources reviewed contain no clinical studies of it for this use.

dermal-rollers-microneedling-eyes.summary: Needling the thin skin around the eyes to trigger collagen production and thicken it, aiming to soften dark circles and a tired look.

quick.overview:
Dermal rollers and similar microneedling tools puncture the skin repeatedly with fine needles. Looksmaxxing communities use them around the eyes hoping to thicken thin skin, soften dark circles and reduce a tired look.

Proponents say the tiny punctures trigger wound-healing and collagen production. Microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy, has been studied mainly for acne scars, wrinkles and hair loss; no trials reviewed examined it specifically for the eye area.
quick.how: Clinicians use handheld rollers and stamping devices, and rollers are also sold for home use. People typically repeat sessions over weeks and combine them with ordinary skincare.
quick.risks: Wikipedia notes safety concerns about non-medical settings where staff lack infection-control training, citing a 2018 New Mexico health warning and a 2024 CDC announcement of HIV diagnoses in three women after microneedling with platelet-rich plasma at an unlicensed spa. The periorbital skin is delicate and close to the eye.

angle.text: Users needle the skin around the eyes to trigger a collagen response, hoping to thicken thin under-eye skin and soften dark circles. Microneedling has been studied for scars, wrinkles and hair loss, with little specific to the eye area.

bates-method-eye-exercises.summary: Early-20th-century relaxation and eye-movement routines promoted to improve eyesight without glasses; reviews find no objective gain in eyesight.

quick.overview:
The Bates method is a set of eye relaxation and eye-movement exercises devised by the New York eye physician William Horatio Bates (1860-1931) and promoted as a way to improve eyesight without glasses. In looksmaxxing circles it sits in the fringe category, where some people hope eye exercises can change how the eyes look or function.

Bates held that focusing errors come from mental strain on the muscles around the eyeball and that relaxation could reverse them. Mainstream ophthalmology and optometry explain focusing through the ciliary muscle and lens, and a 2004 American Academy of Ophthalmology review and a 2005 review of 43 studies did not find objective gains in visual acuity.
quick.how: Techniques include palming (covering closed eyes with the palms), visualising dark objects, shifting and swinging the gaze, and sunning (exposing the eyes or closed lids to sunlight). People practise them as daily routines, often hoping to reduce reliance on lenses.
quick.risks: Critics have raised safety concerns, including driving or working without needed lenses, delaying treatment of conditions such as glaucoma or childhood amblyopia, and retinal or skin damage from looking toward the sun. It is not a regulated medical treatment, and marketers of some Bates-derived programmes have faced legal action.

angle.text: Promoted since the early 1900s, the Bates method uses relaxation and eye-movement routines that followers hope will sharpen vision and reduce the need for glasses. Reviews have not found an objective gain in eyesight, so its link to appearance rests on belief.

hair-bangs-frame-hairstyle-for-eyes.summary: Bangs and face-framing hair that draw attention to the eyes and brow area and reshape how the upper face looks, changed with a haircut.

quick.overview:
Bangs (fringe in British usage) are hair that falls over the front hairline to cover the forehead, usually just above the eyebrows. In looksmaxxing discussions, bangs and face-framing styles are used to draw attention to the eyes and brow area and to change the apparent forehead and face shape. The change shows up as soon as the hair is cut.

Hair covering the forehead changes the visible hairline and frames the upper face; proponents say this shifts attention to the eyes and shortens a long forehead. Formal research is sparse; a 2022 cosmetology paper cited by Wikipedia paired five hairline shapes with fringe styles.
quick.how: People ask a stylist for a cut matched to their hairline and face shape, then style it day to day. Bangs need regular trimming to hold their shape, and they can be grown out if the look does not suit.
quick.risks: Styling carries no significant health risks. Bangs need regular trimming and styling, and the result depends on hair type and hairline.

angle.text: Bangs and face-framing hair draw attention to the eyes and brow area and change how the forehead and upper face look, a visible change from the haircut itself. Claims about eye emphasis have little formal research behind them.

eye-whitening-and-brightening.summary: Efforts to make the whites of the eyes look whiter and less red for stronger iris-to-white contrast and fresher-looking eyes.

quick.overview:
Eye whitening and brightening is about making the sclera (the white of the eye) look whiter and less red so the eyes look fresher and higher in contrast. Users on looksmax.org argue that white, bright sclera matters for every eye colour because of contrast, and especially for brown eyes.

The idea is that a clearer white sets off the iris more strongly. No studies reviewed examine cosmetic eye whitening or its effect on perceived attractiveness, and the sources found are thin.
quick.how: Posters ask about eye drops and ways to reduce redness. Whiter-looking eyes are also commonly linked in discussion to everyday factors like sleep and irritation, which people try to manage.
quick.risks: Wikipedia notes alpha agonist drops used for glaucoma have a higher likelihood of allergic reaction, with burning, stinging and other side effects listed; its eye-drop article does not cover redness-relieving drops in depth. Persistent redness is commonly a reason for medical review.

angle.text: Looksmax.org posters argue that whiter, clearer sclera makes the iris stand out more and the eyes look brighter, especially for brown eyes, and ask about eye drops. Little research targets this goal.

non-surgical-rhinoplasty-liquid-nose-job.summary: Injectable filler used to smooth a bridge bump, lift the tip or add projection without surgery; results are temporary and take effect immediately.

quick.overview:
Non-surgical rhinoplasty, or a liquid nose job, uses injectable filler to reshape the nose without cutting. Practitioners use it to fill depressions, camouflage a dorsal hump, raise the tip angle or add projection, giving a straighter, better-projected profile that is visible immediately.

A filler, most commonly hyaluronic acid gel, is placed in selected points to change contour by adding volume and creating optical straightening. It can only add volume and does not reduce nose size. The literature is mostly retrospective series and reviews, including a case series of 511 procedures over 16 years.
quick.how: It is a short clinic treatment with little or no recovery, appealing to people who want a change without surgery. Results from hyaluronic acid fillers are temporary, and the enzyme hyaluronidase can dissolve them.
quick.risks: The nose's vessels connect with the ophthalmic artery, so accidental intravascular injection can cause skin ischaemia and, rarely, vision loss. Other reported effects include swelling, bruising, asymmetry and granulomas. Regulatory approval of fillers varies by product and use.

angle.text: Filler is injected to smooth a bridge bump, lift the tip or add projection without surgery, with the change visible immediately. Results are temporary, and it is seen as a reversible, lower-commitment alternative to surgical rhinoplasty.

septoplasty.summary: Functional surgery that straightens a deviated nasal septum to open the airway; a breathing operation, often combined with rhinoplasty for shape.

quick.overview:
Septoplasty straightens the nasal septum, the wall of cartilage and bone between the nostrils, when it is bent enough to block airflow. The main payoff is easier breathing. In looksmaxxing forums it comes up because people with a crooked septum ask whether it will make the nose look straighter or should be combined with rhinoplasty or jaw surgery.

The surgeon works through the nostrils, repositioning or removing deviated bone and cartilage. Alone it may not straighten a crooked-looking nose, since the external shape is not the goal. A multicentre prospective study and a 2023 BMJ randomised trial found symptom improvement after septoplasty.
quick.how: It is usually an outpatient operation under local or general anaesthesia, lasting about an hour or less. When people also want the outer nose reshaped, it is performed together with rhinoplasty as septorhinoplasty.
quick.risks: Reported risks include bleeding, septal perforation, septal haematoma, reduced sense of smell, temporary numbness of the front upper teeth, and, less often, a dropped nasal tip or saddle deformity from over-resection. Symptoms can persist or recur in some patients.

angle.text: Septoplasty straightens the inner septum to open the airway, and people discuss it because the realignment can bring small changes in how the nose sits, such as at the tip. Alone it may not straighten a crooked-looking nose, and it is often combined with rhinoplasty.

septorhinoplasty.summary: Combined surgery on the nasal septum and the outer nose, done to improve breathing and reshape a crooked or unwanted nose in one operation.

quick.overview:
Septorhinoplasty combines septoplasty, which straightens the wall inside the nose, with rhinoplasty, which reshapes the outside. It is used when someone has both a breathing problem from a deviated septum and a wish to change nasal appearance, such as a crooked bridge after an injury. The visible result is the new nose shape.

The surgeon corrects deviation and reshapes the nasal cartilages and bones through an open or closed approach, often reusing septal cartilage as graft material. Published research is largely surgical series and trials of peri-operative care rather than comparisons of cosmetic outcomes.
quick.how: It is done under anaesthesia by a licensed surgeon. On looksmaxxing forums people decide between plain rhinoplasty and the combined operation and compare notes on swelling and tip position, which can take months to a year to settle.
quick.risks: Documented issues include bruising and swelling, persisting obstruction (sometimes linked to enlarged turbinates), the need for revision surgery, and anaesthesia-related effects such as sore throat. Outcomes vary by surgeon and anatomy.

angle.text: Septum and outer-nose surgery are done together to fix breathing and reshape a crooked or unwanted nose, and the visible result is the new nose shape. The evidence base is mostly surgical case series.
